Sara — thanks for the estimate. We reviewed the sheet (looks good) and sketched two options that keep your unit economics predictable while giving you downside protection during the pilot. Short summary:

Option A — Marginal-slice (preferred for transparency):
- Breakpoints at 0-25M, 25-100M, 100M+ tokens.
- Marginal discounts only apply to tokens in the higher tier (e.g., tokens 25.01M-100M billed at tier rate B).
- Monthly true-up; no monthly rollforward during pilot (to prevent credentialing complexity), but we can allow a single end-of-pilot smoothing credit.

Option B — Blended ladder (easier invoicing):
- Same breakpoints but blended effective rate across all tokens.
- Simple monthly billing and carryforward allowed up to 1 month during pilot.

Tradeoffs: marginal is cleaner for you if you expect spikes because you only pay discounted rates on post-breakpoint volume. Blended protects your month-to-month predictability but can penalize short-month ramps.

I attached a one-page sketch (DataWell_token_ladder_v2.pdf) with example math using your numbers. Can you confirm which path you prefer, and whether you want the single end-of-pilot smoothing credit for Option A?

Next steps we propose if you pick A: lauren will prepare a pilot SOW with the marginal-slice ladder and marcus will validate billing flow. If you pick B: we’ll lean on standard monthly blended invoicing and a one-month carryforward.

Thanks,
Nikhil Sharma

Sara — following up after internal sync. We recommend Option A: the marginal-slice ladder with a one-time end-of-pilot smoothing credit (capped at 20% of committed dollars). This gives you the favorable marginal economics on spikes while keeping our financial control on rollforwards.

Proposed concrete terms for pilot SOW (3 months):
- Commit: 50M total tokens per month (month 1-3).
- Breakpoints and per-token list price (examples):
  - 0–25M: $0.00080/token
  - 25M–100M: $0.00055/token (marginal rate for tokens in this band)
  - 100M+: $0.00040/token
- Billing cadence: monthly invoicing with monthly true-up.
- Smoothing credit: if end-of-pilot effective spend > committed smoothing threshold, Redwood will issue a one-time credit up to 20% of committed spend to smooth the pilot conversion.
- Contractual: no monthly rollforward; carryforward outside smoothing requires amendment.

Next steps:
1) Sara — confirm you accept Option A semantics.
2) Lauren — I’ll need the SOW draft with those numbers so we can send to procurement.
3) Marcus — please add sample invoice examples to the SOW appendix and confirm the credit calculation logic.

If DataWell is good with these terms we’ll prepare a short SOW + DocuSign link and aim to start the pilot the week after signing.
